title: Strategic fix: i2s mic/speaker shared-bus contention (Parent bus is busy / queues desynced)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of audio truncation + the 'ping instead of speech'. The mic and speaker share ONE i2s peripheral (i2s_audio_bus) at different rates (mic 16k / speaker 48k) and cannot be active simultaneously. When the voice pipeline holds the mic open and an announcement/TTS tries to play, the SPEAKER now loses the race:
  [E][i2s_audio.speaker.std:312]: Parent bus is busy
  [E][i2s_audio.speaker:114]: Driver failed to start; retrying in 1 second (x5)
  [E][i2s_audio.speaker:081]: Event/record queues desynced, restarting speaker task
This is the mirror of the mic-start bug already fixed on the wake path (PR #19 serialised chime->mic). Need the same serialisation for the speaker-vs-mic on the TTS/announcement path: ensure the mic is fully stopped/released before the speaker starts the announcement, and restarted after. Note the graceful on_end recovery (replacing forced_reboot) already prevents the reboots this caused; this bead is about killing the underlying glitch so TTS plays clean.
acceptance_criteria: TTS/announcement plays with no 'Parent bus is busy' / 'queues desynced' errors; GLaDOS spoken responses are not truncated.
notes: 7vd.3 (Kitchen bring-up): Kitchen reboots when HA voice setup runs. Note the 3bq 'real fix' (remove media_player from voice path) is NOT in current assist.yaml — voice_assistant still has 'media_player: my_media_player' (kept deliberately as a vol-0 TTS/completion shim per later comments). on_end no longer force-reboots ('we never reboot'). So a still-rebooting Kitchen is a genuine crash, not the old forced_reboot path — NEED the serial tail during HA voice setup (Guru Meditation/abort/assert/heap/Backtrace + rst: reason) to localise. POSSIBLE side-fix: GLaDOS-only change removed 6 micro_wake_word models (okay_nabu/hey_mycroft/hey_jarvis/alexa/okay_hal/hey_luna), freeing flash+RAM — if the reboot was OOM at pipeline start it may now be gone; user to retest.

title: Arrival flow: fix dead gates (halt_if), snapshot last-played track, add test inject + error logging
description:
Follow-up to esp32-panel-fpo: live arrival 2026-07-03 08:30 fired to the planner but did nothing.

Root causes:
1) ALL api-current-state gates on the Sonos Follow Me tab were built with the condition in the dead 'ifState' field; the current-state node routes ONLY on 'halt_if' (verified empty on all 4). So follow_me-on / person-home / car-home / spotify-playing gates have NEVER blocked. Fix builder to emit halt_if + halt_if_compare + halt_if_type.
2) Design premise wrong: the Tesla ends its Spotify session ~3.5min BEFORE person/device_tracker flip to home (spotify idle 07:27:12Z vs person home 07:30:40Z, car 07:34:49Z), so 'spotify playing NOW' can never be true at arrival. Replace the live-playing gate with a SNAPSHOT: a state-changed node records the last-playing track uri+title+timestamp into flow context; the planner resumes it if fresh (<20min) at arrival.
3) select_source/Connect path is dead: source_list observed None even during Tesla playback. Sonos share-link play_media is the only transfer.
4) Observability/testing: add an inject 'TEST arrival' (bypasses debounce) into the chain; add a Catch node + logger to surface any service-call error on the tab; planners log their decisions.

title: Follow-Me: serialise join→unjoin handover; Arrival: replace dead spotcast.start transfer
description:
Two defects on the Sonos Follow Me tab (46t.17 follow-up):
1) FOLLOW-ME race: planner fires media_player.join and a parallel delayed unjoin. HA sonos join waits up to 30s (WAIT_FOR_GROUPS_TIMEOUT) for the FULL expected group incl. the old coordinator; the unjoin removes that coordinator at +3-5s, so any member joining slower than the delay guarantees 'Timeout while waiting for Sonos player to join the group' (seen 2026-07-03 07:19/07:20). Fix: serialise — join call node completes → delay → fan-out unjoins; join failure now skips the unjoin (music stays put instead of dying).
2) ARRIVAL transfer dead since deploy: spotcast.start does not exist in installed Spotcast v6.0.0-a15 ('Service spotcast.start not found' ~daily since 24 Jun). v6 transfer_playback only targets cast/spotcast entities — cannot address Sonos. Fix: use core spotify media_player.select_source('Kitchen') when the Web API device list contains it, else fall back to Sonos-native play_media share-link of the current track URI. Diagnostics logged to decide long-term path.
Also: williams_room mapped as speakerless (silences nightly planner warn).

title: Album-art online_image OOM-reboots: move image fetch/decode off the panel's internal heap
description:
ROOT CAUSE (2026-06-20, observed flashing 46t.14 Phase A/B). Panel reboots intermittently under album-art load (NOT a clean panic — USB-CDC re-enumerates on reset so the backtrace is lost; serial shows healthy run then the stream drops mid-online_image-decode). It is the hax-class issue resurfacing: INTERNAL DRAM heap exhaustion during cover-art download+decode. Phase A/B climate widgets reduced internal heap headroom enough to tip it from rare to frequent (Phase A borderline-stable, Phase B loops). hax serialiser (cov_pump) + SDIO queue bumps are still merged and correct, but they don't address internal-heap accumulation.

WHY INTERNAL HEAP (not PSRAM, which has 32MB free):
- ESPHome RAMAllocator default = ALLOC_INTERNAL|ALLOC_EXTERNAL|PREFER_INTERNAL (core/helpers.h ~2068). So online_image DECODED buffers (runtime_image) AND the DOWNLOAD buffer (download_buffer.cpp, default RAMAllocator) prefer INTERNAL. Cover decoded buffers fit internal (150x150 RGB565=45KB, 120x120=28KB, 104x104=21KB) so they LAND in internal and accumulate as covers load; np_bg_art 480x480=450KB is too big so it falls back to PSRAM.
- Each download is HTTPS to Spotify CDN (i.scdn.co / mosaic.scdn.co / image-cdn-ak.spotifycdn.com) -> mbedtls TLS needs ~30-48KB INTERNAL per connection (transient spike on top of the decoded buffers). This is the biggest per-download internal cost.
- For JPEG the download buffer resizes to the full JPEG size (online_image.cpp:127). buffer_size (default 65536) is only the initial.
- np_bg_art (now-playing hero, 480x480) is NOT in the cov_pump serialiser and downloads concurrently on track-change (hax close-note flagged this).

STRATEGIC FIX (user direction: serve images another way / through HA):
Proxy + pre-resize covers through HA over PLAIN HTTP on the LAN:
- Eliminates panel-side TLS internal buffers (~40KB/download) — biggest win.
- HA resizes to the EXACT panel size (150/120/104/360) and re-encodes -> tiny JPEGs (~5-10KB) -> small download buffers + fast decode. (Or serve raw RGB565/BINARY so the panel skips JPEG decode entirely.)
- spotify_panel_* sensors emit local proxy URLs (http://192.168.1.3:<port>/cover?url=..&size=150) instead of scdn.co. HA caches.
Implementation: small HA-side resize endpoint (pyscript/AppDaemon/add-on with PIL), or reuse media_player_proxy entity_picture for now-playing.

INTERIM low-risk panel-side levers (stack with above):
- Shrink np_bg_art 480->360/320 (cuts the biggest decode + its download buffer).
- Fold np_bg_art into the cov_pump serialiser (no concurrent big+small decode).
- Shrink cover decoded sizes (150->128, 120->104) to lower per-cover internal footprint.
- Consider vendoring online_image (esphome/components/) patched to ALLOC_EXTERNAL so decoded+download buffers go to PSRAM — eliminates internal accumulation at the root (DMA/decode-perf check needed).
- Add a heap-debug interval (heap_caps_get_free_size INTERNAL + largest block) to MEASURE before/after.

BLOCKS deploying 46t.14 climate Phase A/B reliably (the added widgets are the straw).
notes: Fixed: album art now routed through Tower imageproxy (commit 3a34b16) — fetch/decode moved off panel internal heap, no more OOM reboots. Confirmed working on-device.

title: Runtime crash-reboot under online_image cover-art load: ESP-Hosted SDIO RX buffer assert (sdio_drv.c)
description: Panel (46t firmware, boots fine post-factory-flash) crash-reboots at RUNTIME, ~once per 30-60s, while loading Spotify album/playlist cover art. Captured via Office-PC serial (Nitro-style). Assert: 'assert failed: sdio_rx_get_buffer sdio_drv.c:896 (*buf)' and 'sdio_process_rx_task sdio_drv.c:1260 (copy_payload)', MCAUSE=0x2 (illegal instr) -> rst:0xc SW_CPU_RESET -> Rebooting. Always AFTER 'setup() finished successfully' (not the 46t.13 boot-crash, which is fixed). Pre-crash log: bursts of online_image downloads from mosaic.scdn.co / image-cdn-ak.spotifycdn.com, 'online_image took a long time (1573-5048 ms)', 640x640 JPEG decode to 150x150, Free Heap ~100KB. Root cause: concurrent online_image HTTP downloads saturate the ESP-Hosted SDIO RX path to the WiFi coprocessor; the RX mempool (CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_MEMPOOL_PREFER_SPIRAM:y, in modules/hardware/p4-86-panel.yaml) starves, sdio_rx_get_buffer returns null, esp_hosted asserts instead of back-pressuring. Recovers each cycle but recurs whenever cover art reloads (idle Pick-Music/RECENTLY-PLAYED screen + media browse). Observed 2026-06-20 during 46t.11 validation; my repeated :8080/screenshot captures + a Living-Room clear (-> idle cover-mosaic refresh) likely amplified it, but it will recur in normal music use.
design: Two-level fix. LEVEL 1 (transport, SHIPPED this branch, compile-validated): pin SDIO queue depth in modules/hardware/p4-86-panel.yaml sdkconfig_options — CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_SDIO_RX_Q_SIZE=64 + TX=32 (were Kconfig-default 20). Gives the esp_hosted RX buffer pool headroom to survive the 1.5-5s main-loop JPEG-decode stalls that were draining it to null (sdio_rx_get_buffer assert). Verified ESPHome writes user sdkconfig_options raw/unquoted (RawSdkconfigValue, esp32/__init__.py:2502) so the int lands as =64. REQUIRES on-device confirmation (panel disconnected during this work): reflash via Office-PC USB, load Pick-Music/RECENTLY-PLAYED + browse playlists+artists, watch serial — expect no more sdio_drv asserts. LEVEL 2 (demand, strategic follow-up, needs device): serialise cover downloads so only ONE online_image fetch+decode is in flight at a time, eliminating the burst + decode-overlap that backs up lwip->socket->SDIO. Design: the 8 Pick covers are attributes cover_0..7 of ONE entity (sensor.spotify_panel_playlists) and 8 artist covers of sensor.spotify_panel_artists, so each HA push fires up to 16 set_url at once. Replace per-sensor on_value{set_url} with: store url+want-flag in globals (std::string cov_url[16], bool cov_want[16], int cov_busy=-1); a pump script starts the next wanted download only when cov_busy<0 (call id(pm_cover_img_N)->set_url(...) from a lambda switch on index since online_image ids can't be dynamic in actions); each online_image on_download_finished AND a new on_download_error reset cov_busy=-1 and re-pump. Net: bounded concurrency=1, covers paint progressively. If Level 1 alone stops the crash on-device, Level 2 becomes a nice-to-have (smoother load) rather than required.
notes: RESOLVED + VERIFIED ON-DEVICE 2026-06-20. Level-2 serialisation fix flashed to the panel and stress-tested through the worst case (all 16 covers downloading on boot - the exact load that gave 4 reboots/105s before). Result over 115s serial capture (Office-PC): 0 crashes (no sdio_drv assert, no __cxa_allocate_exception abort, no Rebooting), 1 boot banner (just our reset), setup() finished, all 16 covers fetched+decoded. Serialisation confirmed: 0 back-to-back STARTs (every download START->DONE->START, one at a time); min heap held ~103KB (vs ~94KB-then-OOM before). Panel HTTP endpoint 200, fully operational. The per-decode 'took a long time' warnings remain but are harmless now (no concurrent SDIO/heap pressure). Fix: page-media.yaml cov_pump 750ms interval serialiser + SDIO RX/TX queue headroom (p4-86-panel.yaml). Committed on feature/46t.5-8-functions (PR #36). NOTE for future: now-playing hero art (np_art_img/np_bg_art, page-main) is single-image-on-track-change, not in the serialiser - hasn't caused issues but fold in if needed.

title: 46t.5-8 firmware boot-crashes on device → OTA auto-rollback (assert, illegal instruction)
description:
The 46t.5-8 firmware (PR #36, branch feature/46t.5-8-functions, compiled 2026-06-19 ~23:15) COMPILES GREEN (esphome config valid + full build SUCCESS, RAM 20.8%, Flash 89.7%) but CRASHES on first boot on the physical panel. The ESP bootloader auto-rolled-back to the previous partition, so the panel is SAFE/stable on the OLD firmware. This is a runtime fault the compiler can't catch — it blocks on-device deployment (46t.11).

EVIDENCE (from 'docker exec ESPHome esphome logs /config/frontroom-panel-modular.yaml --device 10.0.20.248', read off the now-running OLD fw which captured the previous boot's crash):
  *** CRASH DETECTED ON PREVIOUS BOOT ***
  Reason: Fault - Illegal instruction ; Crashed core: 0 ; PC: 0x4FF0A79A
  decoded: panic_abort (panic.c:491) <- esp_vApplicationTickHook (freertos_hooks.c:31) <- __assert_func (assert.c:63)
  Reset Reason: exception/panic
  'OTA rollback detected! Rolled back from partition app1'
  'The device reset before the boot was marked successful'
So a C assert() fired during EARLY BOOT (before WiFi/API up). OTA reports 'OTA successful' (bytes written) but the device faults on the subsequent boot before validating -> rollback. Re-flashing the SAME build just crash-rolls-back again (safe, no progress).

REPRO: docker exec ESPHome esphome upload /config/frontroom-panel-modular.yaml --device 10.0.20.248 (1st attempt often spurious 'prepare result timed out' -> retry -> 'OTA successful'); device reboots into app1, crashes, rolls back; then esphome logs (against the old fw now running) shows the crash + rollback.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS - boot-time memory/PSRAM exhaustion: Flash is at 89.7% (near full) and the new firmware constructs ALL lvgl pages at boot, including TWO large lv_canvas on the energy pages (~726KB + ~660KB PSRAM per E1's note in the build) + many online_image decode buffers (album art 240px + up to 16 cover tiles 150px + person photos) + 8 petal PNGs + fonts. A canvas/image buffer alloc returning null -> LVGL/assert abort fits the assert signature. The esp_vApplicationTickHook frame points at the LVGL tick/draw path (first draw on a not-ready buffer).
OTHER SUSPECTS: first on-device run of the 46t.4 widgets (arc/roller/dropdown/canvas/image_recolor) - an LVGL assert in a page's construction or first refresh (np_refresh/mr_refresh/clim_room_refresh/tmr_draw all run on global 1s intervals regardless of active page).

HOW TO DEBUG (serial is required - network/OTA logs CANNOT catch an early-boot crash):
1. Panel is WALL-MOUNTED, OTA-only, NOT on Nitro USB. To get the assert MESSAGE (not just PC), temporarily USB-connect the panel to Nitro (192.168.1.175, ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_aiops simon@; /dev/ttyACM0; ~/esphome-venv/bin/esphome) and run esphome logs over serial while it boots+crashes; OR stty/cat /dev/ttyACM0 @115200 during an OTA-triggered reboot.
2. addr2line -pfiaC -e /data/build/frontroomesp/.pioenvs/frontroomesp/firmware.elf <PCs> (the 23:15 crashing build is still in the ESPHome container build dir). Stored backtrace was shallow (system frames only); serial will give a deeper one + the assert text.
3. Bisect: comment out page packages in frontroom-panel-modular.yaml (start with page_energy, then page_alarm) -> recompile+OTA -> whichever removal stops the rollback localises it. Energy (canvases) first.
4. If memory: shrink/lazy-allocate the energy canvases, cap simultaneous online_image buffers, revisit buffer_size, or defer page construction.

STATE: HA backends already deployed live + working (46t.12 done). PR #36 committed/pushed (compiles green). Only the on-device flash is blocked by this crash. firmware.elf/bin for addr2line are in the ESPHome container at /data/build/frontroomesp/.pioenvs/frontroomesp/.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-20. Root cause: NOT a code/PSRAM bug. OTA only rewrites the app partition, never the bootloader. This build is on ESP-IDF 5.5.4 (boot log: 'ESP-IDF 5.5.4 2nd stage bootloader'); the device carried an older bootloader from a prior baseline, so the OTA-updated app asserted in early boot (esp_vApplicationTickHook -> __assert_func -> illegal instruction) against the stale bootloader and ESP auto-rolled-back. FIX: full factory flash over USB (firmware.factory.bin @ 0x0) rewrites bootloader+partition-table+app together. Done via new Office-PC USB triage host (192.168.1.37, /dev/ttyACM0): esptool --chip esp32p4 write_flash 0x0 firmware.factory.bin. Panel booted clean, setup() finished successfully, connected to HA, stable >1min, app0 self-confirmed (no rollback). The experimental cpu_frequency:400MHz / 200MHz PSRAM / -O2 settings were red herrings - running fine now. Future OTAs of same-IDF builds will work again now the bootloader is current. On-device visual validation now unblocked = 46t.11.

title: Capture top_layer/sys_layer overlays in lvgl_screenshot (opt-in ?overlays=1)
description:
## Goal
The :8080 screenshot endpoint captures the ACTIVE PAGE ONLY — it misses LVGL
top_layer / sys_layer overlays (standard top bar, voice-persona eye, perf HUD,
position dots, Rooms/Playlists + takeover modals). Add the ability to capture
the full composited UI, opt-in via `GET :8080/screenshot?overlays=1` (default
OFF so the existing page-only captures stay clean).

## Why overlays are missing
components/lvgl_screenshot/lvgl_screenshot.cpp (~line 226) captures via
`lv_snapshot_take(lv_screen_active(), LV_COLOR_FORMAT_RGB888)` — it re-renders
ONLY the active screen object. In LVGL 9 the overlays live on separate display
layers: lv_layer_top() and lv_layer_sys(), which that call cannot see.
(Chosen over reading the mipi_dsi framebuffer — Option B — because everything on
this panel is LVGL, and the framebuffer path couples to ESPHome mipi_dsi
internals / double-buffering and is fragile. Layer-composite is self-contained.)

## Approach (Option A — composite the LVGL layers)
In lvgl_screenshot.cpp, when overlays requested:
1. Base: snapshot lv_screen_active() in RGB888 (as today).
2. Snapshot lv_layer_top() and lv_layer_sys() in LV_COLOR_FORMAT_ARGB8888 (need
   per-pixel alpha — empty layer areas are transparent).
3. Alpha-composite in LVGL's draw order base -> top -> sys:
   out = src.rgb*src.a + dst.rgb*(1-src.a)  (premultiply-aware; per channel).
4. Encode the composited RGB888 buffer to JPEG (existing stb path).
- All snapshots MUST run on the LVGL/main task — already handled via the capture
  semaphore in loop(). Keep that.
- Byte order: LVGL stores RGB888 in memory as {B,G,R}; ARGB8888 as {B,G,R,A}.
  Reuse/extend the existing channel-swap logic (LVGL_SS_SWAP_RB). If a composited
  shot comes out R/B swapped or with wrong alpha, that's the knob.
- Memory: ARGB8888 full screen = 720*720*4 ≈ 2.07 MB per layer (PSRAM via
  ESPHome draw_buf handlers). Allocate, composite, free each layer promptly to
  cap peak PSRAM (the file already frees the base snapshot before encoding).
  Skip a layer snapshot if the layer has no children (cheap fast-path).

## Query-param wiring
Find where the component parses `?page=` in the HTTP handler and add `?overlays=`
(truthy = 1/true/on). Default off → identical to current behaviour. `?page=` and
`?overlays=` compose (switch page, settle, then composited capture, restore).
If a config-level default is wanted, add an Optional bool in __init__.py
(CONFIG_*), but a pure query param is enough and keeps the engine config minimal.

## Files
- esphome/components/lvgl_screenshot/lvgl_screenshot.cpp  (capture + composite + query parse)
- esphome/components/lvgl_screenshot/lvgl_screenshot.h     (signatures if needed)
- esphome/components/lvgl_screenshot/__init__.py           (only if adding a config default)

## Validate / build / flash
- cd esphome && make validate DEVICE=kitchen-panel-modular.yaml   (schema/codegen)
- make compile DEVICE=kitchen-panel-modular.yaml                  (full C++ build; ~10 min)
- OTA flash BOTH dev panels (they carry capture_mode on after o5p):
    docker exec ESPHome esphome upload /config/kitchen-panel-modular.yaml   --device 10.0.20.183
    docker exec ESPHome esphome upload /config/frontroom-panel-modular.yaml --device 10.0.20.248
- On-device check: curl ':8080/screenshot?overlays=1' on each; confirm the top
  bar (clock/battery/cog) + any active overlay appear, alpha looks right, no R/B
  swap. Compare ?overlays=1 vs default (overlay absent) for the same page.

## Public-fork sync
components/** is the MECHANICALLY-SYNCED part of the public fork
(f00lycooly/waveshare_esp32-86-esphome). After merge, run:
  scripts/sync-public.sh --push
(secret-scans + pushes the byte-identical component). No module hand-port needed.

## Follow-up (optional, separate)
Re-capture screenshots/ overlay variants (e.g. main+topbar) once it works, and
note them in screenshots/README.md. Not required for this bead.

## Context
- Builds on esp32-panel-o5p (display-capture standardised; both panels now
  carry capture_mode on). See bd memory esphome-package-merge-capture.
- Vendored component is a local LVGL-v9 port of dcgrove/esphome-lvgl-screenshot.
- Front Room IP 10.0.20.248, Kitchen IP 10.0.20.183. ESPHome container on Tower;
  build/flash via esphome/Makefile (warm tmpfs toolchain).

Option A implemented in components/lvgl_screenshot/{cpp,h}: ?overlays=1 snapshots lv_layer_top()+lv_layer_sys() in ARGB8888 and alpha-composites over the base RGB888 in draw order (base->top->sys); default off so page-only captures unchanged. Empty layers skipped; each layer freed promptly (peak = 1 ARGB layer at a time). Straight-alpha (LVGL_SS_PREMULTIPLIED_OVERLAY=0) + existing LVGL_SS_SWAP_RB. make validate+compile clean for kitchen & frontroom; OTA-flashed both (Kitchen 10.0.20.183, Front Room 10.0.20.248). title: Kitchen: BLE proxy (BT-over-C6) hard-blocks loopTask at enable → boot loop; disabled as workaround
description:
Kitchen P4-86 panel (7vd.3): with ble_proxy enabled, the panel boots, runs setup() fully, then loopTask hard-blocks inside 'esp32_ble: Enabling' (BT controller enable over the C6/esp-hosted link) → task_wdt at ~5s → boot loop. DEFINITIVELY Kitchen-binary-specific: the Frontroom binary (same ble-proxy module) enables BLE on the SAME panel/C6 and boots fine, and the C6 does WiFi+BT for Frontroom. WORKAROUND APPLIED: ble_proxy include commented out in kitchen-panel-modular.yaml (panel now boots, WiFi+HA work). 

LEADING HYPOTHESIS: BLE-enable timing race — Kitchen has fewer components than Frontroom, finishes setup faster, and calls esp_bt_controller_enable before the C6 BT side is ready; the call blocks >5s (wdt) instead of failing/retrying. Frontroom's heavier setup delays BLE-enable until the C6 is ready. (Coprocessor version RPC also returns 'unknown' on both, benign.) 

TO RESTORE BT ON KITCHEN: investigate delaying/gating the esp32_ble enable until the esp-hosted link is up (e.g. enable_on_boot:false + a delayed enable, or gate on C6 readiness), then re-enable ble_proxy. Frontroom keeps BLE meanwhile. Related: [[3bq]] is a different audio issue, not this.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-29: BLE restored on Kitchen and auto-enables ~15s after boot, verified on-device (clean boot → switch off→on → panel stays connected, no loop). Design: esp32_ble enable_on_boot:false (boot always clean + OTA-safe) + esphome.on_boot one-shot switch.turn_on after 15s + manual 'Bluetooth proxy' switch. Root cause was a C6-BT-readiness race at boot, not memory or a permanent BT-over-C6 failure. Front Room unaffected (keeps boot-enable; its heavier setup avoids the race). In PR #70.

ROOT CAUSE (esphome/modules/page-climate.yaml): the arc drag write path IS debounced (clim_room_commit mode:restart delay 700ms) and the HA echo IS locked out via clim_user_editing — BUT the edit-lock release is racy. At :187-189 the clim_target_temp on_value handler clears clim_user_editing the moment ANY incoming echo lands within 0.25 of the CURRENT clim_target: 'if (editing) { if (|x-clim_target|<0.25) editing=false; else return; }'. The Vaillant lags several seconds and emits multiple stale temperature echoes. Mid-drag the finger passes through/near the device's last-reported setpoint -> an echo matches -> lock CLEARS -> the next stale echo passes the now-open lock, enters the else branch (:196-199), sets clim_target=<stale device value> and calls lv_arc_set_value(stale) (:207) -> the knob snaps back; the next drag event sets it to the finger again -> oscillation. The arc (:654-687) has NO on_press/on_release, so 'editing' is inferred per-value-change and released by proximity, which is inherently racy against a laggy backend.

STRATEGIC FIX: bracket the drag with arc on_press/on_release. Set clim_user_editing=true on PRESS and hold it for the entire touch; do NOT release on value proximity while pressed. On RELEASE, fire the commit and only then open a confirm window that clears the lock when HA confirms our value (keep the existing 0.25 confirm + the 60s clim_edit_release safety). While clim_user_editing (or pressed), echoes must never call lv_arc_set_value. This removes the stale-echo-vs-finger feedback loop. Verify on next flash by dragging slowly through the current setpoint.
notes: VERIFIED on-device 2026-06-26: drag smooth (press/release bracket), no mid-drag jump, AND Boost-cancel now resyncs the dial to the device setpoint immediately (82h.7b: clim_last_dev_temp cache + resync on boost->non-boost). PR #53.

title: Alarm Who-picker person photos blank: uzd.18 one-shot fetch with no re-arm on picker open
description:
REPRO (on-device, post-uzd flash 2026-06-26): open alarm Who-picker → person photos are blank boxes (Simon/Rosie/William). Spotify cover lists work.

PROVEN NOT THE CAUSE (verified this session):
- Proxy URL the panel builds resolves: GET http://192.168.1.3:8088/120x120/http://192.168.1.3:8123/api/image/serve/<id>/512x512 -> HTTP 200, image/jpeg, 8425B.
- That JPEG is BASELINE, 120x120, 3-component YCbCr (ESP-decodable; not progressive).
- HA serves person.{simon,rosie,william} entity_picture = /api/image/serve/<id>/512x512 (200).
- Code wiring all correct: page-alarm on_value builds URL + sets cov_url/cov_want[20..22]; page-media pump imgs[20..22]=al_who_*_img; widgets image{src: al_who_*_img} + show on_download_finished / glyph on_error; buffer_size 65536, format JPEG/RGB565/resize 120x120.

ROOT CAUSE: person-photo fetch is BOOT-ONLY / one-shot with no retry or re-arm. cov_want[20..22] is set ONLY by the person entity_picture on_value handlers (page-alarm.yaml:197-225) — i.e. at HA-connect or when entity_picture changes. The pump (page-media.yaml:548-561) clears cov_want[i] BEFORE issuing the fetch and never re-sets it on failure, so a single lost/starved/failed fetch (e.g. starved behind the 0..19 cover burst while cov_inflight churns + 12s self-heal at boot) leaves the slot permanently unfetched. Crucially, al_who_refresh (page-alarm.yaml:701, run by al_who_open when the picker opens) only repaints selection-ring borders — it does NOT re-arm cov_want[20..22]. So opening the picker never (re)triggers the fetch. This is a regression from uzd.18, which replaced the previously self-retrying direct set_url with a fire-once want flag. (imageproxy only logs errors, so its access log can't confirm/deny the panel request.)

STRATEGIC FIX: re-arm cov_want[20..22] (from the cached cov_url, or rebuild from the person sensors' last values) inside al_who_refresh so opening the Who-picker always (re)fetches — self-healing + naturally lazy (only fetch person photos when the picker is actually shown, aligning with uzd.7's lazy-load direction). Guard against re-fetch storms (only re-arm if the slot isn't already decoded/inflight). Verify on next flash by opening the Who-picker cold.
notes: VERIFIED on-device 2026-06-26: person photos render. Real cause was missing lvgl.image.update in on_download_finished (download+decode succeeded per DIAG logs); picker-open re-arm kept as resilience. PR #53.

title: Now Playing clings to stale paused target; does not auto-follow the actively-playing group
description:
REPRO (on-device, post-uzd flash 2026-06-26): No group actively playing (most paused). Panel shows Living Room cover art (LR went paused ~35 min ago). Start music in Kitchen → panel STAYS on Living Room art; the corner room chip still says Living Room. Opening the group picker correctly shows the only currently-playing group is Kitchen.

ROOT CAUSE (by design, = the 46t.17 gap): the panel's now-playing binds at compile time to ONE fixed mirror entity sensor.front_room_active_media (homeassistant/templates/frontroom_panel.yaml), which merely reflects whatever input_text.frontroom_active_player names. That helper has initial: media_player.living_room (homeassistant/input_text.yaml) and is ONLY written on a manual device-tile tap / group-picker selection (active_player_sync / media_target_sync in page-media.yaml:599-624). Nothing updates it when a DIFFERENT group starts playing, so the mirror clings to the last-selected (now paused) player. The group picker is correct because it reads live sensor.sonos_topology directly, not the locked mirror — hence the divergence.

DESIRED BEHAVIOUR: auto-adopt — when the panel's current target is idle/paused (or unavailable) and exactly one other group is actively playing, the panel should follow that playing group (update input_text.frontroom_active_player / media_active_target + chip + art). Ambiguity (multiple groups playing) should fall back to an explicit SEE/SWITCH affordance rather than guessing. Candidate implementations: (a) HA-side automation that repoints the helper to the active coordinator when the selected target goes idle; (b) panel-side: derive a 'playing coordinator' from sonos_topology g0..g3 blobs and adopt it when room_state[target] is paused/idle. Keep manual selection authoritative once the user explicitly picks a room (don't yank control mid-listen).

title: Rooms modal Group action ignores removals + coordinator change (no playback transfer)
description:
REPRO (on-device, post-uzd flash 2026-06-26): Play in Living Room → add Kitchen (Group) → group OK. Re-open Rooms modal (pre-stages [LR(coord), Kitchen]); DESELECT the controller (Living Room) leaving staging=[Kitchen], which the UI correctly tags as the new controller; hit Group. EXPECTED: music transfers to Kitchen, Living Room drops. ACTUAL: Kitchen goes silent, music continues in Living Room. The cover-art room selector then shows Kitchen while the group picker correctly reports Living Room as the live coordinator — control target and live group have diverged; tapping Living Room in the picker re-syncs.

ROOT CAUSE (esphome/modules/page-media.yaml:1441-1493): the Group on_click only does ADDITIVE joins + a narrow 'free a stuck coordinator' unjoin. With staging=[Kitchen]: (1) the free-coordinator check (:1458-1475) sees Kitchen is a member (room_coord==0 && room_size>1) and UNJOINS Kitchen — the room we wanted to KEEP — silencing it while LR (coordinator) keeps playing; (2) the additive join (:1479-1493) needs size>=2, so with one staged room it is SKIPPED. The modal pre-stages from live topology (prestage_from_topology) presenting itself as a group EDITOR, but the action never reconciles: (a) REMOVALS — rooms in the live group but de-staged (Living Room) are never unjoined; (b) COORDINATOR CHANGE — when staged index-0 changes (LR->Kitchen) playback is not migrated to the new coordinator.

STRATEGIC FIX: make Group reconcile the staged set against the live group: unjoin de-staged former members; when the coordinator (index 0) changed, transfer playback to the new front (drop old coordinator via unjoin so Sonos keeps the rest playing on the retained member, or re-coordinate) BEFORE/alongside joining; keep the additive path for size>=2. Also reconcile media_active_target only to a room that is actually in the resulting live group so the control target cannot point at a silenced room.

comments.text: FIX IMPLEMENTED + DEPLOYED (2026-06-26, branch bugfix/sonos-multiroom-reconcile-autofollow, commit 432083a). page-media.yaml btn_group on_click rewritten as a true reconcile: reads live group members from sonos_g[] (blob holding the staged front), unjoins every de-staged former member (unjoining the old coordinator => Sonos promotes a remaining member, playback continues), then additive-joins staged set under staged.front (size>=2) to re-coordinate a swap, then re-points active_media_player/media_active_target + helper at staged.front. Removed the old free-stuck-coordinator block (bug cause #1 — it unjoined the kept room). esphome config + full compile clean; OTA-flashed (boots clean). PENDING on-device: confirm unjoining the coordinator promotes a remaining member and keeps playing. comments.text:
SENIOR-UX RESEARCH (subagent + frontend-design skill, 2026-06-21). Full deliverable:

== 1. CURRENT STATE ==
Two media surfaces, one front-room-locked target. main_page (Now Playing) = full-bleed hero (art + title/artist + tap-overlay: transport, vertical volume, Pick/Browse/Rooms quick-launch). multiroom_page = 6 room rows + a 25% now-playing mini-dock. The Rooms modal (top-layer on main_page) is the only true multi-room surface: a 7-tile staged-select grid committing media_player.join/unjoin. Topology sensor drives only small playing-dots; it never surfaces what's PLAYING (title/art) elsewhere, and "switch which group I control" is conflated with "edit grouping" in one modal.
Decoded state|n|n = <state>|<is_coordinator 0/1>|<group_size>. is_coordinator = group_members[0]==self; group_size=len(group_members). It's per-ROOM, not per-GROUP — no attribute says "these 3 rooms are one group playing X".

== 2. DATA RE-MODEL → sensor.sonos_topology (generic, per 46t.16) ==
Rename front_room_sonos_topology → sonos_topology (GLOBAL/shared; every panel reads same system view). front_room_active_media stays PER-PANEL but parameterised ${panel_id}_active_media.
(a) Per-room (extend): living_room: "playing|1|3|55|kitchen,office" = state|isCoord|size|vol%|members(csv,coord first). Adds vol% + members so a tile shows its volume and resolves its group without cross-referencing 7 attrs.
(b) Per-GROUP now-playing (NEW — the missing piece): one attr per active group g0..g3:
   g0: "living_room|playing|Living Room + Kitchen|Black Hole Sun|Soundgarden|<arturl>" = coordSlug|state|groupLabel|title|artist|artUrl ; g_count:"2".
Pipe-delimited, art URL last (longest). Panel splits on |, fetches art via existing imageproxy cov_* serialiser (4 covers within the 20-slot pump; reuse slots, no concurrency). This makes "see everywhere at a glance" ONE sensor read vs seven. Keeps rooms (grouping/volume) vs groups (now-playing) cleanly separated.

== 3. THREE UX APPROACHES ==
A — "Controlling: <Group> ▾" switcher on Now Playing (minimal). Hero unchanged; source line becomes a tappable chip → compact group-picker (cards from g0..g3, art thumb, ● selected) + "Idle rooms/Edit groups" card → existing Rooms modal. SWITCH=tap group card sets ${panel_id}_active_media→coordinator. Reuses hero/np_* overlay/resolver/Rooms modal. PRO smallest delta, keeps the strong hero, clean switch-vs-edit split. CON "see everywhere" is one tap away; grouping touched in 2 places.
B — Rooms Overview grid replaces multiroom_page. 2x3/2x4 grid of group/room cards = mini-now-playing (art thumb + state glyph + title/artist + inline vol bar); grouped rooms collapse to ONE card; ●ctrl ring marks controlled; idle rooms dim. [edit]→Rooms modal. tap card→controls that group; full transport on hero (one swipe). PRO best at-a-glance, fixes h99 (row/dock overlap), per-card vol, no scroll. CON 8 cells dense (live ~4-6 after grouping); art thumbs ~120px heap budget; transport not on this page.
C — Group-management takeover (Sonos "System" model). Top: horizontally-paged group cards (now-playing + group/master volume); bottom: checkbox room list with per-room vol (☑=in group, live join/unjoin to the paged coordinator). PRO most complete (see+switch+group+trim in one). CON highest cost + densest; LIVE checkbox grouping risks yanking a Spotify stream (needs 4eq.23 confirm popup); most divergent from current code.

== 4. RECOMMENDATION ==
Ship A + B together; defer C's live-grouping. Adopt B's Rooms Overview grid as the multiroom_page replacement (delivers "see everywhere" + retires h99) + A's "Controlling ▾" hero chip so the hero is honestly multi-group. Keep the EXISTING staged-select Rooms modal as the dedicated edit-grouping surface behind [edit] (already built/verified 4eq.20; staged-commit is SAFER than C's live checkboxes). Three-verb split: SEE=overview grid (B, fed by g*) ; SWITCH=tap card/hero chip (A)→${panel_id}_active_media ; CONTROL=hero transport + per-card/hero volume, edit grouping via modal. C is the north star; revisit once g* + overview proven on-device.
IMPL SURFACE: homeassistant/templates/sonos_topology.yaml (rename generic; add per-room vol%+members; add g0..g3+g_count; update producer + homeassistant/Makefile; coordinate 46t.16). frontroom_panel.yaml → ${panel_id}_active_media. page-main.yaml: replace multiroom rows/dock with card grid + Controlling▾ chip + group-picker takeover; new topo_g0..g3 text_sensors; route group art via cov_* serialiser. page-media.yaml: keep Rooms modal as [edit]; update topo_* parsers; add per-room vol% slider. Reuse media_active_target resolver, imageproxy pump, join/unjoin blocks.

== 5. RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS ==
- g* group identity churn: Sonos coordinator ordering unreliable (4eq.22). Sort groups by coordinator SLUG (not group_members[0]) so g0 stays stable frame-to-frame. DECISION: OK to sort groups alphabetically by coordinator for stable card slots?
- Attribute 255-char cap: g* with title+artist+art URL can approach 255 (Spotify art URLs long). Publish bare art PATH, let panel prefix imageproxy host. Confirm worst-case length vs live data.
- Per-room vol% source: needs volume_level per room in template; confirm all 7 players expose it when idle/unavailable (default last-known or --).
- Take-over confirm (4eq.23): switching control / live-grouping a playing coordinator can yank a Spotify stream. Overview "tap to control" is read-safe, but any GROUPING action should get the deferred Take over/Stop/Cancel popup. DECISION: wire 4eq.23 before/with this?
- 46t.16 sequencing: this work wants the generic sonos_topology rename — recommend bundling the rename here, leaving weather/per-panel parts to 46t.16.
- Card density vs heap: 4-6 group-art thumbs ride the same online_image path that caused pm1.19 OOM. Size ≤120px, keep on the one-at-a-time cov_* pump, verify int_free headroom on-device.

title: GLaDOS raster asset plan: split static chassis from live eye

comments.text:
REFINEMENTS (review + user direction 2026-06-17):

1. IDLE CAMEO must be in the coordinate contract. The screensaver shows GLaDOS scaled to ~216px tall, top-right (in line with the clock), NOT the centred active size. Contract must record eye-centre/bbox at BOTH placements: active-centred (~260x440) and idle-cameo (~130x220 top-right). Tracked by new idle bead.

2. HEAD MOVEMENT — PRESERVE IF AT ALL POSSIBLE (user priority). Eye-only/static head is the LAST-RESORT fallback, not the default. Preference ladder:
   (a) BEST: retain smooth head tilt/thrash via PPA-accelerated transform (pm1.13) applied to the REDUCED layer (raster chassis is far smaller/cheaper to transform than today's full LVGL object tree).
   (b) GOOD: coarse discrete pose-swap image set — N pre-rendered tilt/thrash chassis frames, swap the image per behaviour (cheap blit, gives real head movement, just not tweened). Budget ~230KB/RGB565 pose.
   (c) LAST RESORT ONLY: eye-only animation in a fully static head.
   dw5/spq should design so (a)/(b) stay open — do NOT bake assumptions that forbid head motion.

3. Front mask likely SKIPPABLE: recessed-socket design has no chassis occluding the eye except the live lids. Start without it.

4. Asset source: render the chassis straight from the APPROVED mockup .superpowers/.../glados-motion.html (headless screenshot) so the baked asset is pixel-identical to what the user signed off.

5. Carry-forward: the live optic widgets + lerp/behaviour engine + phase/persona/colour wiring already built in pm1.4/pm1.5 survive spq — only the static shell/bezel/cavity/bellows geometry becomes an image.

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text:
CONTRACT DELIVERED (design workflow cross-checked): esphome/assets/images/GLADOS_RASTER_CONTRACT.md.

KEY FINDING (corrects the naive plan): chassis->image removes only 1 of 3 motion costs (the 11 gradient rounded-rect into-layer draws). The dominant motion costs are (B) the SOFTWARE transform-blit of the whole va_head layer (unchanged by the swap) and the live-eye shadow_width blooms. So clean FPS needs the FULL lever set, not just the image.

SHIP-NOW (spq + initial pm1.14, one firmware change):
 L1 chassis->image (1 image replaces 6 chassis widgets in va_head)
 L2 shadow-gating while moving (zero iris/aperture/pupil shadow_width during motion, restore on settle)

ESCALATE only if on-device motion measurement still core1-bound:

 L6 identity-placement cameo (pm1.14: native 120x216 asset at absolute x/y, identity transform -> no layer -> dirty-area redraw; biggest idle win)

Movement priority preserved: ACTIVE face keeps full smooth tweened motion; IDLE cameo is eye-only by design (pm1.14).

title: Perf instrumentation: publish FPS + per-core CPU% as HA diagnostic sensors
Platform perf: execute_from_psram=false (move code/rodata off the PSRAM bus)

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text:
POINT C MEASURED — REGRESSION on this board. execute_from_psram=false (vs Point B baseline exec=true, 15% buffer, SIZE): loop_time 33->50-55ms (+60%), cpu0 17->47-49% (~2.8x), cpu1 5->18%, free_psram 22.79M->28.72M (+5.9MB, code+rodata left PSRAM = confirmed effective), heap/block flat, fps~1 static. 

CONCLUSION: flash XIP is SLOWER than executing from 200MHz PSRAM on this eng-sample P4 (flash at default speed/mode). The desk hypothesis (PSRAM-exec is a perf sacrifice) is wrong for THIS hardware. The hypothesised upside (less PSRAM-bus contention w/ scanout) only manifests under heavy redraw load, unmeasurable on a static screen, while the code-speed penalty applies always. 

OPTIONS: (1) revert — keep execute_from_psram=true (B already moved the draw buffer off PSRAM, the main contention source); (2) try flash_freq 80MHz + QIO/OPI to make XIP competitive, then re-test; (3) defer decision until measurable under animation load (pm1.4+). Recommend (1) now, (2) as a separate experiment.

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text: DECISION: drop this lever. execute_from_psram=false is a measured regression on this board (Point C: loop_time +60%, cpu0 ~2.8x) because flash XIP @ default DIO/40MHz is far slower than octal/200MHz PSRAM. Flash-speed rescue (bump to 80MHz) was attempted but is NOT cheaply achievable: the flash-freq Kconfig choice is ignored unless sdkconfig is regenerated fresh, and a fresh regen drops CONFIG_BT_ENABLED on this P4-hosted-BLE config (esp_bt_defs.h missing) — destabilising the build for an unproven gain. Keeping execute_from_psram=true. pm1.2 (draw buffer -> internal SRAM) already addressed the primary PSRAM-bus contention. Closing won't-do.

title: Display DMA flush to offload CPU (MIPI-DSI/LVGL buffer path)
description: Investigate and enable DMA for the display flush path so pixel push doesn't burn CPU that the GLaDOS animation needs. Review the current esp32_p4 / mipi_dsi display + LVGL buffer config (buffer count/size, full vs partial refresh, PSRAM vs internal draw buffers, double-buffering, bounce buffers). Confirm whether flush already uses DMA; if not, configure it. Measure CPU/FPS delta with the perf-monitor overlay before/after. Watch for PSRAM bandwidth contention on the P4. Strategic, not a patch: get the buffer/DMA architecture right rather than shaving individual redraws.

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (desk phase, on Tower):

1. DMA flush is ALREADY enabled and not user-configurable. mipi_dsi.cpp hardcodes DMA2D for the flush path (esp_lcd_dpi_panel_enable_dma2d / use_dma2d=true), driving MIPI-DSI from a single PSRAM scanout FB (num_fbs=1). No YAML knob exists — the bead's 'if not, configure it' resolves to already-on. Flush blocks on a binary semaphore (io_lock_) until on_color_trans_done, so the calling task yields (not busy-spin).

2. Real lever = LVGL draw-buffer placement (configurable via buffer_size). Was 100% → ~1MB buffer forced into PSRAM (lvgl_esphome.cpp only attempts internal SRAM when frac >= 1/4 screen; 100%→frac1 skips internal). Result: every flush DMA2D-copies PSRAM(draw buf)→PSRAM(FB) while the DPI peripheral continuously reads PSRAM for scanout — three-way PSRAM-bus contention (the P4 bottleneck the bead flags).

CHANGE: ui-shared.yaml buffer_size 100%→15% (frac 8 → ~130KB → fits internal SRAM). Render in fast internal RAM; flush reads internal→writes PSRAM, taking the draw buffer off the PSRAM bus. PARTIAL mode (full_refresh off) unchanged, so smaller buffer = more cheap DMA chunks, not more CPU. Build validated (esphome config OK).

INSTRUMENTATION: perf-overlay.yaml debug sensors (free heap / largest block / loop_time / free psram) flipped internal:true → entity_category:diagnostic so before/after is measurable via HA API (HUD shows CPU/FPS but screenshot endpoint skips top_layer, so can't be read remotely).

PENDING (on-device): OTA flash (reboots panel) + verify boot log has NO 'Failed to allocate … internal draw buffer' (else fell back to PSRAM = no-op), confirm free PSRAM jumps ~1MB, read loop_time/FPS/CPU delta.

Recovery requires reconciling the key (reflash with HA's key, or reconfigure the HA integration with the new key). Reading HA's stored noise_psk from .storage was denied (correct). title: HA sensor: Sonos group + playing-state topology (for Rooms modal)
description:

- A 'default context room' helper: the currently-playing coordinator if any (for first-load room context), else media_player.living_room.

Keep it resilient to unavailable entities (default 'idle'/empty). VERIFY in Developer Tools after deploy + Template reload.

title: Controlled fleet esp_hosted C6 slave upversion (OTA slaves first, then raise host pin)
description:
Move the panel fleet (Front Room, Kitchen, Hallway) from esp_hosted 2.12.1 to a newer slave/host pair, deliberately and in order, when we want newer C6 firmware. NOT urgent — current 2.12.1 baseline is stable.

Procedure (per the esp-hosted-slave-upversion-order memory):
1. Panel UP on current host (2.12.1): OTA the C6 slave to target version via the esp32_hosted update: entity (manifest esphome.github.io/esp-hosted-firmware/manifest/esp32c6.json). C6 fw persists across P4 reflashes.
2. Verify each C6 reports the new version (HA update entity / serial).
3. Raise the framework pin espressif/esp_hosted==<target> and reflash each P4 so host==slave.

Do per-panel; do NOT bump the host pin before the slave is confirmed upgraded (cold-boot host>slave = boot loop, ref 7vd.3). Also revisit whether the per-panel esp_hosted_spec override scaffolding is needed at all (currently removed; fleet shares the hardware-module ==2.12.1 pin).
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-06-29 (Kitchen, esphome 2026.6.2, host pinned 2.12.1): the planned 'OTA slave first via the esp32_hosted update entity, then bump host' path is BLOCKED by ESPHome design.

1) update entity caps slave <= host. esphome/components/esp32_hosted/update/esp32_hosted_update.cpp fetch_manifest_(): 'Only consider versions <= host library version ... to avoid upgrading coprocessor ahead of host'. With host 2.12.1, update.kitchenesp_esp_hosted_firmware reports latest=2.12.1 and will NEVER offer the C6 a 2.12.9 slave. So slave-first-via-update-entity is impossible while host stays 2.12.1.

2) Chicken-and-egg: host-first (bump host->2.12.9 with slave still 2.12.1) boot-loops before the update can run (GetCoprocessorFwVersion RPC was EXTENDED in 2.12.2; a 2.12.9 host sends RPCs the 2.12.1 slave can't parse -> 'Response not received' -> loopTask stall -> wdt). Boot loop = OTA cannot recover -> USB only.

VIABLE PATHS to 2.12.9:
 a) Embedded-mode update: set update: platform esp32_hosted type=embedded with the 2.12.9 network_adapter_esp32c6.bin (sha256 9d8cec9dcca632e9ded31de555a5b49c70316d30b87ae06bd933fd35a5a11513) — embedded mode compares the embedded bin's version (not the <=host manifest cap), so it WILL offer 2.12.9; host stays 2.12.1 (host<slave is tolerated), trigger install -> slave 2.12.9, verify, THEN bump host pin to 2.12.9. BUT app partition ~87% full (~1.35MB free) and the C6 bin is ~1.5MB -> likely WON'T FIT without freeing flash.
 b) USB-flash the C6 slave to 2.12.9 directly (recovery path, see memory c6-slave-provisioning-before-p4), then bump host. Works but physical USB, not OTA.

ISOLATION FLAG (confirmed): CONFIG_ESP_HOSTED_MEMPOOL_PREFER_SPIRAM is a NO-OP on 2.12.1 (the 2.12.1 esp_hosted component does not define the Kconfig; buffers sit in internal RAM). It only goes live on 2.12.8+. So the FIRST 2.12.9 build should set use_psram:false to keep buffers in internal RAM = identical to the working 2.12.1 baseline, isolating the version change. Re-enable + validate PSRAM buffers separately afterwards.

VALUE ASSESSMENT / RECOMMENDATION: HOLD on 2.12.9 unless a specific driver appears. 2.12.1 works fleet-wide; internal RAM is at 18-21% so the main P4 upside (PSRAM mempool) is unneeded; the rest of 2.12.2->2.12.9 is SPI-HD/Zigbee/OpenThread/IDF6 fixes irrelevant to our SDIO+WiFi+BT path. Only safe route is USB C6 flash on Kitchen first. See memory esp-hosted-slave-upversion-order (the slave-first ordering rule still holds; this note adds WHY the update-entity can't do it).

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text: MOTIVATION / on-device measurement (post spq, 2026-06-18): the ACTIVE voice phases (listening/thinking/responding) sit at ~80-90% core-1 / ~7.5 fps on device — the talk-thrash continuously transforms the whole head and LVGL software-rasterises the transform-BLIT every frame (the chassis->image swap cut the per-frame DRAW but NOT the blit). This is the documented ~7fps P4 software-transform ceiling. PPA (this bead) is the only lever to push active animation smoother (~40% -> ~12fps) while keeping smooth motion. NOTE: that 80-90% was partly inflated by a concurrent debug-log stream (2nd API client); a clean perf-only re-measure was set up but not yet captured (user cleared context). IDLE is already clean (8% settled) after the overlay-invalidation fix in spq.

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text: Audit (wf_ae066685) finding: PPA is doubly dead for the active blit. Beyond the LV_USE_PPA=0 hard-disable (needs ESPHome lvgl fork), lv_draw_ppa.c gates the image draw-unit to scale_x==256 && scale_y==256 && rotation==0 — it REJECTS the scaled va_head blit (scale 1.20). So PPA cannot accelerate the active transform at all; it only helps IDENTITY blits, i.e. only AFTER pm1.17 (L5) lands. Deprioritise: PPA is at most a small bonus on an already-identity head, not a path to 30fps.

title: Media perf: hardware JPEG decode for album art (online_image, P4 JPEG codec)

comments.author: Claude Code (Tower)
comments.text: FINDING: online_image JPEG decode uses the JPEGDEC software lib (bitbank2/JPEGDEC 1.8.4). Its SIMD optimisations are ESP32-S3 (Xtensa) only — on the RISC-V P4 it runs as plain software decode. The P4's hardware JPEG codec peripheral is NOT integrated into ESPHome's online_image/runtime_image; using it would require a custom external_component wrapping esp_jpeg_decode, not a config toggle. Cost is a transient CPU spike on track-change only (not steady-state animation), so this is lower-value/higher-effort than the other campaign levers. Recommend deferring until after the steady-state levers (pm1.8/pm1.9) are measured. Server-side resize/pre-decode is a cheaper alternative if track-change jank shows up in profiling.

title: Media: album cover art on primary player
description:

1. online_image (id: album_art): format JPEG, type RGB565, resize ~220x220, on_download_finished + on_error triggers. Decode buffer in PSRAM (hex 200MHz — ample, ~97KB).
2. Source the entity_picture from the SELECTED player (4eq.16). Simplest: read entity_picture via the same HA template-mirror sensor 4eq.16 introduces for state/title, prefixed with ${home_assistant_host}. entity_picture is a relative HA proxy URL with embedded token + per-track cache-buster, so re-fetch is automatic; no extra auth.
3. lvgl image: widget in media_primary, src album_art.
4. Fallback: empty entity_picture (radio/no art) OR on_error → hide image, show MDI speaker glyph. Never crash.
5. Verify: esphome compile + RAM/Flash delta; confirm real on-device fetch/decode.

DE-RISKED: http_request: already declared in hardware pkg (waveshare-esp32-p4-86-panel.yaml:38); PSRAM ample; display 720x720.
